hoisting_lesson: naming the context members (context->viewport) initially BROKE getViewport: 160 B instead of 148, because MSVC re-loaded the pointer for each of the four getActual* calls instead of hoisting it once. The fix is a hoisted local - `const void* viewport = context->viewport;` - which is both byte-exact and still readable. A raw-offset read written inline happened to force the hoist, so the raw form looked "more exact" for a misleading reason.
outline_rect2d_note: outlineRect2d is the six-argument renderer draw overload: draw(2, x0, (height()-1)-y0, x1, (height()-1)-y1, &color) - the leading literal 2 is a mode the reference unit carries as `2`, and the thick parameter is genuinely unused. First attempt scored 79 with both sizes at 138; the single difference was SCHEDULING: the original loads the rect's four components BEFORE the renderer pointer and in DESCENDING offset order (y1, x1, y0, x0), so the source has to read them into named locals in that order first. Reordering the statements - not the expressions - was the whole fix.
reordering_lesson: two of this class's methods were decided purely by STATEMENT ORDER rather than by expressions: outlineRect2d needs the rect components read before the renderer, and getViewport needs the viewport pointer hoisted into a local (inlining context->viewport costs 12 bytes because MSVC reloads it per call). When sizes match but scores do not, look at the instruction schedule before suspecting the source form.
g3d_api_asymmetry: G3D::Vector2 exposes float x, y as PUBLIC DATA FIELDS (G3D/Vector2.h line 42) while G3D::Rect2D exposes x0()/y0()/x1()/y1() as ACCESSOR METHODS - so p0.x and rect.x0() respectively. Getting this backwards is a C2064 "term does not evaluate to a function taking 0 arguments" / C3867 pair of errors.
line2d_note: line2d is the same five-argument renderer draw as outlineRect2d minus the leading mode literal: draw(p0.x, (height()-1)-p0.y, p1.x, (height()-1)-p1.y, &color), with the color passed BY POINTER. The reference unit src/2008-06/0066fa50.cpp wraps its body in #pragma float_control(precise, off, push) / pop - a per-function override; this unit already carries the global #pragma float_control(precise, off) that the vendor AdornG3D.cpp uses, so no extra pragma was needed.

reference_availability.finding: the mined corpus is not uniformly packaged. A unit is portable only if it carries its body INLINE (the "// Make this compile to the exact bytes below" form, or the short struct-form ones). Units ending in "// roc-lib: <lib> <file>.cpp" point at a companion file that this workspace does not contain - a recursive search for those names returns nothing. Always read the last line of a unit before assuming a reference body exists.
portable_here: prepareRenderPass 00670d50 (542-line inline body) - needs the Ogre 1.4.5 particle API and the node maps at +0xb8/+0xf4

explosion 00675360 (4379 B, 1659-line inline body) - portable but NOT cheap: it is a full Ogre scene-graph method. Its reference asserts sizeof(Ogre::SceneNode)==552, sizeof(Ogre::Quaternion)==16, sizeof(Ogre::Matrix3)==36, sizeof(Ogre::MemoryDataStream)==52, sizeof(std::map<Ogre::String,Ogre::SceneNode*>)==32, and members on its own class: cache at +0xb8, nodes at +0xa0, rotation at +0x114, translation at +0x138. Treat it as a from-scratch batch.
reference_availability.consequence: the eight already-ported methods are everything that can be cheaply ported from this workspace. The draw primitives would each be a from-scratch decode against the Ogre 1.4.5 headers - feasible but a batch each, and box/sphere/quad/cylinderAlongX are 931-1734 bytes with C++ EH frames. The single highest-leverage fix remains the header decision.

prepareRenderPass.reference: src/2008-06/00670d50.cpp is from server: 100% by king_originala; roc-cl 21022; roc-flags /O2 /Ob2 /Oi /Oy /GF /GS- /EHsc /MD /fp:fast
prepareRenderPass.binding_note: the reference unit named its stand-in class method updateParticleBudget (private, non-virtual). Renaming the declaration AND the definition to the public virtual prepareRenderPass is all that was needed - the body is untouched and byte-identical. The ONLY other change was to the stand-in class layout: a public virtual function makes MSVC insert its own vfptr at +0, so the reference's own offsetof asserts (total 0x44, first 0xb8, second 0xf4) shifted by 4 and failed with C2118 negative subscript. Padding the class with an explicit void* __vfptr member at +0 and shrinking the unobserved00 array from 0x44 to 0x40 kept every asserted offset while the second implicit vfptr landed at +4 - which is why 0x3c, not 0x40, is the correct pad.
prepareRenderPass.what_it_does: reads a cached memory query through a cdecl helper at 00678510, derives a particle budget limit (5000 below 60 MB, 10000 by default, 12000 above 300 MB), sums the particle quota of every system attached to the two SceneNode maps at +0xb8 and +0xf4, and when the sum exceeds the limit rescales quota, emitter velocities and durations and finally clamps the accumulator to the limit.

lessons: a reference unit's placeholder name is only ever a rename away from the real symbol: bound the method by renaming the declaration AND the definition, then let the compiler tell you what the class layout has to be (C2118 negative subscript is the loudest possible signal that a vfptr just moved every offset).

when an exact unit and a merged unit disagree by a fixed byte count and the first divergence is in the prologue, stop comparing bodies and compare environments: the exact trial had no pragma, no base class and complete stand-in types. Five body-level hypotheses (including one retracted pow diagnosis) all missed it.
